title: Manager Transition and Feedback Integration Handbook
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary:
This handbook defines the standard process for promoting, hiring into, or transitioning employees into manager roles at Redwood Inference and how managers should integrate continuous feedback into team operations. It is intended for new managers, hiring managers, people-ops partners, and people-leaders who support role transitions. The goal is to shorten manager ramp time, reduce rework from poor handoffs, and create predictable, equitable performance feedback cycles across teams.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: provide a repeatable, evidence-based sequence for manager activation and establish a standard feedback integration loop that ties 1:1s, performance check-ins, and calibration cycles to development outcomes.
- Scope: applies to all people managers (IC->Manager transitions, IC hires into manager roles, and lateral manager transfers) across engineering, product, and GTM teams. Excludes executive hires (VP+), which follow separate onboarding and exec enablement.

Intended audience:
- New and existing managers at Redwood
- People-ops partners and HR business partners
- Hiring managers and onboarding sponsors
- People managers' skip-levels and org leaders for calibration

Key principles:
1. Evidence-first: Early goals and feedback should be tied to observable behaviors and artifacts (1:1 notes, project plans, release retros).
2. Asynchronous-friendly: Support distributed teams with templates and clear async handoffs.
3. Manager as multiplier: Prioritize actions that increase team productivity, retention, and career growth.
4. Equity and consistency: Use standard rubrics and calibration inputs for reviews and promotions.

Owner and responsibilities:
- People-ops: owns the handbook, templates, and calibration timetable.
- Hiring manager / Sponsor: owns the first 90-day operational plan and introduction to stakeholders.
- Manager's manager (skip-level): owns manager enablement cadence and quarterly calibration evidence review.
- Buddy / peer manager: owns day-to-day practical orientation (systems, meetings, norms).

Transition types and quick guides:
- Promoted-in-place (IC -> first-line manager): 90-day focus on delegation, hiring needs, 1:1 structure, and time allocation.
- External hire into manager role: 60-day discovery + 90-day execution with upfront stakeholder alignment.
- Lateral manager transfer: 30-day stabilization then 60-day optimization, with documentation-driven handoffs.

First 0–30 days: Stabilize and observe
1. Pre-start (people-ops + sponsor):
   - Complete access checklist (repo read, payroll, benefits admin) before day 1.
   - Send welcome packet with org map, team mission, and initial reading list.
2. Week 0–1: set expectations
   - Day 1: 30–45 minute skip-level intro scheduled by sponsor.
   - Day 2: manager completes the "Team Intake Form" (see appendix) documenting immediate priorities and open roles.
   - Schedule standing 1:1s with direct reports and a 1:1 rhythm for the first 90 days (recommended 30–45 minutes).
3. Observation tasks (complete by day 30):
   - Join at least one full planning or sprint ceremony for each direct report team.
   - Read three recent project retros and two incident reviews relevant to the team.
   - Shadow cross-functional partners (product, infra, sales) for context.

Deliverables by day 30 (owner in parentheses):
- Team Intake Form (Manager)
- 90-day manager plan draft (Manager + Sponsor review)
- Access and tooling checklist confirmed (People-ops)

Days 31–90: Align and act
- 30–60 day goals: hiring prioritization, delegation experiments, first coaching cycle, and initial candidate slate if hiring.
- 60–90 day goals: run first team-level retro focused on process improvements and present a progress update to skip-level.

Concrete actions and templates:
- Delegation experiment (2–4 weeks): pick one recurrent task to delegate to each direct report, document expected outcome, and run a short feedback loop.
- 1:1 agenda template (suggested):
   1) Quick pulse (1–2 min)
   2) Priorities and blockers (10–20 min)
   3) Development and career conversation (5–10 min)
   4) Feedback for manager (2–5 min)
- Manager daily/weekly time allocation targets:
   - 40% people time (1:1s, hiring, coaching)
   - 30% operational/strategy (roadmaps, prioritization)
   - 20% stakeholder syncs and cross-functional work
   - 10% learning and admin

Performance and feedback integration loop (quarterly cycle)
1. Continuous inputs (ongoing): 1:1 notes, project artifacts, onboarding surveys, stakeholder feedback, incident/retro notes. Store evidence links in the manager's evidence folder (People-ops will provide a template).
2. Mid-quarter check-in (manager-led): short, documented conversation with each direct report documenting progress against agreed outcomes.
3. Quarterly calibration packet (for manager): include 3–5 artifacts per direct report (project deliverables, peer feedback, and manager observations) and a calibrated rating suggestion.
4. Calibration meeting (people-ops facilitated): managers present packets; HR and people-ops moderate to ensure consistency and equity.

Calibration meeting structure (60–90 minutes per cohort)
- Pre-meeting: packets submitted 7 days prior.
- During meeting: each manager gets 5–7 minutes to present 3 highlights and one development area per person.
- Mechanism: use rubric scores (See section: Rubrics and evidence) and document consensus ratings in the central calibration sheet.
- Post-meeting: people-ops publishes calibration outcomes and action items within 3 business days.

Rubrics and evidence (summary)
- Four dimensions to score: Delivery (D), People (P), Strategy & Execution (S), and Impact (I).
- Each dimension scored on a 1–5 scale with examples for each level.
- Evidence required: at least one artifact per dimension for promotion or rating >4.

Equity guardrails:
- Blind artifact review option: reviewers can opt to anonymize candidate names in artifacts for higher-risk promotion reviews.
- Disparate impact check: people-ops runs a simple check for distributional anomalies (by tenure, team, manager) during calibration rounds.

Manager enablement and support programs:
- First 90 days: weekly cohort workshop run by people-ops covering delegation, difficult conversations, hiring, and time management.
- Ongoing: quarterly manager learning days and a manager buddy program (peer pairing for first 6 months).
- Escalation path: manager has direct access to People-ops Lead (email and pager) for urgent people issues; use escalation template in appendix.

Operational checklists and templates (table)
| Item | Owner | When | Required evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Access & Tools Onboarding | People-ops | Pre-start | screenshot of tool access & Okta entry |
| Team Intake Form | Manager | Day 2 | completed intake doc link |
| 1:1 schedule | Manager | Day 5 | calendar invite export |
| Delegation experiment plan | Manager | Day 30 | short plan and success metrics |
| First retro report | Manager | Day 75 | retro notes and action list |

Sample 1:1 feedback request email (template)
Subject: Quick 1:1 feedback request
Hi <name>,

I’m trying a short feedback practice to help me be a better manager. If you have 5 minutes before our next 1:1, could you tell me: 1) what I should start doing, 2) what I should stop doing, 3) what I should continue doing? I’ll summarize and share actions. Thanks for helping me improve.

Best,
<Manager name>

Performance improvement and remediation guidelines:
- Informal coaching: documented in 1:1 notes with a clear timeline (2–8 weeks) and success criteria. People-ops must be notified when informal coaching begins.
- Formal performance plan: escalation to people-ops and the manager's skip-level; document objectives and monitoring cadence. Templates are provided in the appendix.

Measurement: Manager success metrics (examples)
- Team engagement pulse score (target: >= 4.0/5 after 90 days)
- Time-to-ramp for direct reports (target: 60–90 days for role competency)
- Retention within direct reports over 12 months (target: >= 90%)
- Hiring cycle time for approved roles (target: 6–8 weeks from req approval to offer)

Asynchronous handoffs and artifacts (minimum required)
- Handoff checklist: open tickets, status of key projects, hiring pipeline, recurring meeting notes, and one-sheeter describing team priorities.
- Evidence folder: links to project artifacts, incident timelines, and peer feedback used in calibration.

Security and systems access notes:
- Managers must complete role-based security training within first 14 days.
- Access to sensitive HR systems (performance sheets, salary bands) is role-limited; request through People-ops with documented business justification.

Appendices
A. Team Intake Form (fields): team mission, top 3 goals (90 days), people inventory, active hires, immediate risks, dependencies, short-term success metrics.
B. Delegation experiment example: engineering manager delegates on-call rotation rebalancing and measures runbook completion time and incident MTTR.
C. Promotion evidence checklist: artifacts mapped to rubric dimensions, endorsements, and timeline.
D. Escalation template (email): quick form to notify People-ops Lead including summary, affected people, timeline, and requested assistance.
